about: Keys of Dolphin's per-game settings (vendor/dolphin/Data/Sys/GameSettings) that the core build keeps and embeds at /dolphin-sys/GameSettings (tools/gamesettings-filter.mjs). Every other key is left out: add one only with its reason and, when it can change speed or what the game shows, a measurement.

keys.why: Correctness: games that need address translation run wrong without it. Under the MMU the block JIT refuses every block (jo.memcheck) and no region is translated or installed (0091), so those games run correct on the cached interpreter.
keys.measured: No effect on the measurement disc (its [Core] section is empty).

keys.why: Correctness: FPSCR.FPRF is computed from FP results only when the setting is on (patch 0121, as upstream's JITs; every tier of ours follows it, the interpreter included). Games that read FPRF ask for it in their INI.
keys.measured: No effect on the measurement disc (its [Core] section is empty). Costs FPRF updates in the games that set it.

keys.why: Correctness: games that need a safer texture cache hash more samples of each texture (or all, 0) so updates to texture memory are seen. VideoCommon reads it on the CPU side, the same on every backend (the rendering agent checked wgpu, 2026-10-22).
keys.measured: No effect on the measurement disc (its INI sets no [Video_Settings] key). Larger values cost CPU time in the games that set them, as on Dolphin desktop.

keys.why: Correctness: False keeps the XFB copy to RAM for the games that read it back. Under video=wgpu the copy is skipped unless the game's settings ask for it (#93), so without this key those games lose their frames.
keys.measured: No effect on the measurement disc (its INI sets no [Video_Hacks] key). The RAM copy costs what it costs on Dolphin desktop, in the two GameCube games that ask for it.

keys.why: Correctness: True lets the CPU read the EFB (peeks: colour and depth under the cursor, lens flares, picking). Off, every peek is skipped and reads 0 on any backend. Under video=wgpu peeks read back through the staging texture (0093); software reads its own EFB.
keys.measured: No effect on the measurement disc (none of its INIs is kept). Peeks cost a staging readback per 64-pixel tile touched (cached until the next draw), only in the 14 GameCube discs that set it.

keys.why: Correctness: False writes EFB copies to guest RAM too, for the games that read them back (CPU-side effects, screenshots, recursive textures). Without it those games sample stale RAM. Software and wgpu both honour it (ramcopy homebrew).
keys.measured: No effect on the measurement disc (none of its INIs is kept). Its cost, forced on the race scene under wgpu + aot=1 (race-perf, 3 valid pairs, 2026-10-24): useful frames 59.1 -> 47.3/s (XFB copies per VI 0.98 -> 0.79), VI p99 22 -> 61 ms, while CPU and GPU both keep headroom (max speed 2.0 and 3.5): the readback's latency, not its throughput. Paid only by the 36 GameCube discs that set it; software always copies to RAM.

keys.why: Correctness: the games that read the bounding box (pixel engine registers) get the real box only with it on: off, BoundingBox::Get returns the value the game wrote. The software renderer computes the box as it rasterises; video=wgpu has no GPU box yet (SWBoundingBox, never updated by the GPU path), so a disc that sets it is a software-only case for the renderer choice.
keys.measured: No effect on the measurement disc (none of its INIs is kept). Software computes the box as it rasterises either way; the key only makes Dolphin return it (6 GameCube discs).

keys.why: Correctness: False makes each EFB copy to RAM wait for the GPU before the CPU goes on, for the games that read a copy back at once; deferred (Dolphin's default), they may read RAM before the copy lands. Only matters with EFBToTextureEnable=False; software copies synchronously either way.
keys.measured: No effect on the measurement disc (none of its INIs is kept). Its cost, forced on the race scene under wgpu + aot=1 with EFB copies to RAM (~780 a second; race-perf, 3 valid pairs, 2026-10-25): useful frames 50-55 -> 21/s (XFB copies per VI 0.84-0.92 -> 0.35), the GPU side becoming the limit (max speed 5.4-6.0 -> 1.35): each copy waits for its own readback (~2.5 ms). Paid by the 12 GameCube discs that set it with EFBToTextureEnable=False, as correctness asks; software copies synchronously either way.
